Welcome.Intro: **Mod WARNO and Steel Division 2 without the copy-paste.** Describe a change once, such as "double the range of every autocannon", and EasyNDF applies it to every matching object in the game's `.ndf` files.
Welcome.Map.Mods: Import a mod, or build your own **rules**
Welcome.YourFilesNeverLeave: Your files never leave this computer, and your originals are never changed. Export your mod to keep a copy of your rules.
Welcome.Tour.Tip: A hands-on tour that makes a small mod with you; nothing is exported
Welcome.ThisWindowIsOn: This window is on the Help tab.
Tour.Needed: The rest of the tutorial needs this step. Do what it asks to go on.
Tour.Wait: Wait while the rules run. The tutorial goes on after.
Tour.About.Files: Where the game files you change come from; a sample file is added for you
Tour.About.ModsAndRules: Make a mod, and a rule set for the sample file
Tour.About.Rules: Write a rule, condition and action, that changes the sample file
Tour.About.PreviewAndExport: Run the rules, read what they changed, and see what Export would write
Tour.About.Editor: Read the file, its tips, and the lines your rules change
Tour.About.Armory: Units, their values, their 3D models, divisions and weapons
Tour.Files.Start: This tutorial makes a small mod with you. **Nothing is exported.**
Tour.Files.Source: **Source** picks your game or a mod; [[Add Its Files]] lists its files once one is picked. Here the tutorial uses **Sample Data**.
Tour.Files.Add: [[Add Files…]] and [[Add Folder…]] add .ndf files from anywhere.
Tour.Files.Sample: The tutorial added its **Sample Data**: an **Ammunition.ndf** with 29 weapons' ammunition.
Tour.Mods.Start: A mod is a set of rules. Each rule finds parts of the files and changes them, as many as it matches.
Tour.Rules.Start: Now write a rule: what it looks for, and what it changes.
Tour.Mods.List: Your mods. All the ones switched on run, the top one first.
Tour.Mods.Letters: Lit **D B U W** letters: the mod changes Divisions, Battlegroups, Units or Weapons.
Tour.Mods.Plus: Click [[+]] to make a new mod.
Tour.Mods.Name: Name it **Tutorial Mod**, then click [[OK]]
Tour.Mods.RuleSets: Rules are kept in rule sets. A rule set changes the file in its name.
Tour.Mods.EditItem: Click **{item}**, the most common kind: it changes values.
Tour.Mods.RuleName: Replace **New rule** with **Longer autocannon range**, then click [[Next]]
Tour.Mods.Scope: **Applies to Each descriptor**: the rule looks at every descriptor in the file.
Tour.Mods.Gate: **Any**: one condition met is enough. **All** needs every condition met.
Tour.Mods.Scan: **Property scan** reads the file, so the windows can list its values' names.
Tour.Mods.OpenCondition: **Double-click** this line: the condition. It picks which descriptors change.
Tour.Mods.ConditionValue: In **Value**, type **AutoCanon**, then press [[key:Escape]] to close the list of names.
Tour.Mods.OpenAction: **Double-click** this line: the action. **(no target)** means no value is picked yet.
Tour.Mods.ActionTarget: In **Target**, pick **MaximumRangeGRU**, the ground range. Typing **MaximumRangeG** jumps to it.
Tour.Mods.ActionValue: In **Value**, type **1.5**: the range (in GRU, the game's distance unit) × 1.5.
Tour.Preview.Start: Now run the rules, and see what they change.
Tour.Preview.Run: Click [[Preview]]. The rules run; nothing is saved.
Tour.Preview.Status: The **Status** column says what the rules did to each file.
Tour.Preview.OpenDetails: Click **Details** to open the Details panel.
Tour.Preview.Details: **Details** lists every change, before and after.
Tour.Preview.Where: **Export to**: the folder the files would be written to.
Tour.Preview.Which: **Files**: only changed ones, all of them, or the selected.
Tour.Preview.Options: **Options**: how the files are written. The defaults are fine; [[?]] explains each one.
Tour.Preview.WillWrite: Every file it would write, new or replacing one.
Tour.Preview.Cancel: Export stays off in the tutorial. Click [[Cancel]]
Tour.Preview.RealExport: Outside the tutorial, Export writes the files to your mod's folder, ready for the game.
Tour.Editor.Start: The Editor shows a file's text, and what your rules change in it.
Tour.Editor.Text: Files receive syntax highlighting. **Hover over a word**, such as **MaximumRangeGRU**, for information about it.
Tour.Editor.ShowExport: Click [[Show Export]]: the file as your rules change it.
Tour.Editor.Changes: Click [[Changes Only]]: just the lines your rules change.
Tour.Editor.Changed: The autocannons' **MaximumRangeGRU**, × 1.5, each with your rule's comment.
Tour.Editor.OpenTree: Click this button to open the **Descriptor Tree**.
Tour.Editor.Tree: Every descriptor in the file. **Click one** to list its values, then click [[Next]]
Tour.Editor.Properties: **Properties**: the values of the descriptor you clicked.
Tour.Armory.Start: The Armory shows every unit and weapon of the game.
Tour.Armory.Source: Pick **WARNO** under **Source**. Its units take about half a minute to read.
Tour.Armory.Cards: Every unit, with its main values.
Tour.Armory.Views: These show the units as cards or as a table.
Tour.Armory.Find: Type a name, such as **Abrams**, then click [[Next]]
Tour.Armory.PickUnit: **Click a unit** to see its values.
Tour.Armory.Values: Its values. Changes made here are saved in the mod open on the Mods tab.
Tour.Armory.Model: **Drag** to turn the model; the mouse wheel zooms.
Tour.Armory.ModelSide: Its turrets, and the weapons on each.
Tour.Armory.DivisionList: **Click any division** to see its units, and how many cards of each, then click [[Next]]
Tour.Armory.Battlegroup: Its Official Battlegroup: the ready-made deck the game offers, card by card.
Tour.Armory.WeaponList: Every weapon the units carry, with its damage and range.
Tour.Armory.Done: That's the tutorial. Each tab's [[?]] button explains it in full.
Tour.Mods.Comment: Tick **Comment**: each value the rule changes gets a comment beside it.
Tour.Mods.CommentOriginal: Tick **Original value**: the comment says what the value was.
Tour.Mods.ActionNote: This note is for advanced targets, such as list items. This rule doesn't need it.
